title: Dictionary pattern C - Latest record per entity
summary: Coding / Python / Dictionaries / Grouping and state

children.text: Keep the latest record for each entity_id. Input is not sorted. updated_at values are comparable timestamps in one time basis. On equal timestamps, keep the last input record.

items: Store the first record for an unseen key.
Use >= to implement the stated last-input-wins tie rule.

children.text: The dictionary stores the best record seen so far for each key. Update only when the candidate wins under the defined timestamp and tie policy. The sample uses numeric timestamps; arbitrary date strings must be parsed and normalized before comparison.
Stable sorting then overwriting gives the same tie behavior, but costs O(n log n) time and O(n) temporary storage.
Single pass: expected O(n) time and O(k) retained references for k entities. Missing or incomparable timestamps require an explicit validation policy.

children.title: Watch for this
children.text: Unconditionally overwriting the value works only when input ordering guarantees the newest record comes last.

items: How would you change the policy to break ties using a stable sequence_id instead of input order?
Transfer keyed accumulation to conditional state.
Make ordering and tie assumptions explicit.
